title: perf(canary): automated detection of latency/throughput regressions + rollout guards
author: Aisha Clarke
description:
Motivation: reduce manual work and risk when rolling model/runtime changes by automatically detecting small latency/throughput regressions during perf canaries and enforcing rollout guards. This PR implements an automated detector that evaluates canary realtime metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency and qps) against a rolling baseline, computes a regression score, and wires that into the rollout controller to prevent automatic promotion when regressions exceed configured thresholds.

What changed (high level): added a detector service (perf/canary/detector.py / pkg/canary/detector.go) that ingests canary metrics, computes baseline statistics using a rolling-median+MAD approach, and emits a single regression_score metric. Integrated that signal into the rollout controller so canary -> canary promotion is blocked if regression_score > threshold for N consecutive windows (configurable), with hysteresis and automatic rollback hooks. Exposed configuration in the Console API and a CLI flag for private installs. Added unit & integration tests and docs.

Why this approach: we want fast, robust detection that tolerates noise (MAD), adapts to workload changes (rolling baseline), and avoids flapping (hysteresis & consecutive-window checks). The detector is lightweight and can run colocated with canary workers or as a centralized service depending on deployment.

Key behaviors: 1) baseline: rolling median over last 7 successful canaries (configurable) and MAD for dispersion; 2) detect: compute percentage delta on p95 and qps and convert to a single regression_score weighted by latency impact; 3) thresholding: default threshold 0.10 (10% regression) and default consecutive_windows=2; 4) hysteresis: once blocked, require 2 contiguous passing windows to clear (configurable); 5) SLI/alerting: emits canary.regression_score and canary.regression_status (pass/warn/fail) and generates audit log events for rollouts blocked by perf.

Testing: unit tests for detector metrics logic (tests/perf/test_canary_detector.py), end-to-end integration test that simulates traffic and verifies guard blocks a rollout with synthetic latency increases, CI includes perf-canary-integration job that runs a short load profile.

Operational notes: default rollout behavior remains unchanged for existing customers. New rollout guard is opt-in at account level; org admins can enable via Console -> Rollouts. For Dedicated/Private customers, the installer exposes flags: --canary-detector-mode={local,central} and --canary-threshold.

Security/Compatibility: no new external network dependencies by default (detector can run locally). Backwards compatible with existing rollout APIs.

Follow-ups (future work): model-aware weighting (prioritize latency regressions on tail-sensitive models), auto-tuning of thresholds using historical regressions, and dashboard visualization for regression_score time-series.

review_comments: Diego Morales: Can the threshold be made per-deployment instead of org-wide? In high-latency regions teams might tolerate higher deltas.
Aisha Clarke (author): Yes — made threshold and consecutive window values configurable at rollout-scope and org-scope; Console UI now shows scope. See console/api/rollout_config.yaml change.
Evan Chen: The MAD-based dispersion looks good, but I want an explicit p99 check in case of tail regressions; can we add p99 as a secondary gating metric?
Aisha Clarke: Added p99 to the weighted regression_score (p99 weighted 1.5x p95). We keep overall score as single scalar for the rollout controller to evaluate.
Priya Nair: Tests flaked on CI (integration job) first run due to resource limits; re-ran the job and it passed — consider adding a short warmup to the runner.
Aisha Clarke: Added a warmup sleep + retry in the integration test harness and reduced synthetic load to avoid resource contention. CI job stable now.
merge_details: Merged by Priya Nair using squash merge. Merge title: 'perf(canary): automated detection of latency/throughput regressions + rollout guards'. PR closed and changelog updated.
release_notes: Introduce automated canary regression detection and rollout guards: emits canary.regression_score, blocks promotions if regressions exceed thresholds, configurable scope and hysteresis. Opt-in via Console or installer flags.
notes: Default threshold is conservative (10%); admins should tune per workload.
Integration job intentionally short — full verification should run in nightly perf suite.
Monitoring: add an alert for canary.regression_status == fail to paging for oncall SRE if org-level guard is enabled.
